property_summary: After a Collect call, the balance of msg.sender remains non-negative (no underflow).
After calling Collect, the contract's total balance (sum of all account balances plus ether held by the contract) remains unchanged if Collect did not actually transfer any ether to the caller.
After a Collect call that reverts, the state variable MinSum remains unchanged
After a successful Collect call, the balance of the caller does not exceed the contract's total balance at the time of the call plus the value sent in the same transaction.
After Collect, the caller's balance in the mapping never exceeds the sum of its previous balance and the msg.value sent in the same transaction.
After a successful Collect call, the contract's balance should decrease by exactly the amount collected.
After any successful Collect call, the unlockTime for the caller must have been at least the original unlockTime that was set at the time of the last Put.

If Collect succeeds, then after Collect, the unlockTime for the caller must be a timestamp that is at least the maximum of the caller's previous unlockTime and the Put's _unlockTime (or block.timestamp) that was set when the caller last called Put.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp if they had at least one Put before that collect.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime must not have decreased due to a subsequent Put that sets unlockTime to a smaller value.
Collect can only be called when block.timestamp is strictly greater than acc.unlockTime.
Collect can only succeed (not revert) when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime, not when equal.
Collect does not revert when block.timestamp >= acc.unlockTime, but reference C reverts when equal.
Collect does not reduce balance when block.timestamp equals acc.unlockTime
Collect reverts when block.timestamp equals acc.unlockTime, but the buggy version allows it to succeed.
Collect() allows withdrawal when account balance equals the requested amount (acc.balance == _am) under reference, but mutant requires strictly greater.
After a successful Collect call when account balance equals the requested amount and conditions are met, the contract's balance decreases exactly by the requested amount.
After a successful Collect call with _am equal to account balance, the caller's balance increases by _am.
When Collect withdraws the exact balance of the sender (acc.balance == _am) and other conditions hold, the call succeeds (does not revert) in the reference, but the mutant reverts.
When Collect is called with _am equal to the sender's balance, the call does not revert.
When the sender's balance equals MinSum, Collect should succeed if other conditions are met, but the mutant requires strictly greater than MinSum, reverting the call.
When the sender's balance equals exactly MinSum, the Collect transaction succeeds under the reference but reverts under the mutant who requires strictly greater.
When a user's balance equals MinSum and all other conditions are met, Collect always succeeds, but the mutant requires strictly greater.
When the caller's balance equals MinSum, the Collect function should succeed if the other conditions (balance >= _am, time > unlockTime) are met.

For any user with balance equal to MinSum, Collect should succeed when collecting an amount less than or equal to balance and after the unlock time; the mutant reverts, so the rule is that the call does not revert.
After Collect, the balance of the caller is acc.balance + _am; but the reference ensures it is acc.balance - _am, so the invariant that balance never increases upon Collect holds only for reference.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract should decrease by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After a successful Collect call, the total balance sent back to the caller (msg.value sent in the Collect call) must not exceed the caller's original balance in the contract.
The caller's balance in the contract should never increase after a Collect call.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract should be the previous balance minus the amount withdrawn.
After any sequence of operations ending with a Collect call, the contract's balance must be at least the sum of all user balances recorded in the Acc mapping.
After Collect(uint256) returns without revert, the caller's balance in Acc does not decrease by more than the amount withdrawn.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the caller's Acc.balance never decreases by less than the amount withdrawn
After Collect(uint256) reverts if the caller's balance is less than the amount requested, but the mutant never reverts (always executes the transfer).
After Collect(uint256) the caller's Acc.balance must be non-negative.
